payload.detail: CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN 2026-09-20; NO LONGER PARKED. This is not a flaky test — it catches a real phone defect that also hits clinicians. The Differentials mode-nav row (49px) paints IN page flow, then ModeNavHeaderPortal moves it into the fixed phone header at ~315ms; content loses that height and every element rises 49px. usePhoneOverlayChromeReserve only republishes the measured 121px at ~423ms, so for ~110ms the whole page sits 49px too high. A press that straddles that correction lands on one control and releases on another: recorded trace shows pointerdown on the compare-open link at y 492-540, pointerup at the identical y hitting "Edit selection" because the link had moved to 443-491, and the browser retargeting the click to their common ancestor. The link never activates — no error, no navigation. scrollY is 0 throughout, so this is layout, not scrolling, and Playwright hit-target checks cannot see it because press and release were each individually on a real element. EVIDENCE: 0/41 reproductions through the repo runner (10x alone, 10x under 4 busy loops, 20x under 12, plus a full shard) — shard load is not the right kind of slowness. Under Chrome DevTools renderer throttling: 0/10 at 4x, 10/10 at 10x, 9/10 at 20x, and 0/10 at 10x when the phone chrome is allowed to settle first. That last row is the control. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW. (1) It is the PHONE click that fails, not the desktop one. tests/ui-tools.spec.ts:2928 is the test declaration; the test contains two compare-open clicks, and the URL CI recorded has no q=Pain, which matches the 390x844 phone block. Above the phone breakpoint the reserve publishes 0px and no addon row mounts, so desktop is not exposed. (2) The TO-UNBLOCK suggestion in this row does not work and is refuted: the destination "Loading presentation" role=status skeleton cannot be the settle signal, because it lives inside the destination route and only renders AFTER the URL commits. Proven by holding the destination response 20s — urlChangedAfterMs 20130, loadingSkeletonSeenAfterMs null. The "racing an unhydrated link" hypothesis is the right family but the wrong mechanism: the link is a plain next/link anchor from a Server Component, so a pre-hydration click would still navigate natively. The race is hydration-driven LAYOUT, not handlers. STILL OPEN AFTER PR #2929 — READ THIS BEFORE CLOSING THE ROW. PR #2929 (publishPhoneOverlayChromeReserveNow, called from both portals) closes this only for IN-SESSION navigation, and NOT for the cold page.goto the trace above was taken on, which is the path CI fails on. The publisher refuses to act until the reserve hook has settled a value at least once — it must, because before that responsive layout can still report the wide 200px stack (#147) and publishing that would move content twice. React runs layout effects children-first and the hook belongs to the shell, so on a cold load a portal effect ALWAYS runs before the hook has settled and the immediate publish is suppressed, every time. Established by adversarial review of #2929 and independently reproduced; pinned as failing-when-fixed cases in tests/phone-overlay-reserve-portal-wiring.dom.test.tsx, which is also the only coverage of the portals wiring at all — every case in tests/phone-overlay-chrome-reserve.dom.test.ts calls the publisher directly and would pass with both useLayoutEffect blocks deleted. A second gap: unmounting a portal does not shrink the reserve, so content sits 49px too LOW instead; a cleanup cannot simply publish, because React runs layout-effect destroys before it detaches portal children. THE WAY OUT, not yet built or verified: have the portal publish its OWN height as a delta to the reserve currently in force instead of re-measuring the whole stack. That removes the #147 exposure, and with it the settle precondition, and it gives the shrink direction naturally via the effect cleanup. It is a real change to shared phone chrome on every route and needs its own browser evidence — verify:phone-chrome plus the Playwright settle assertion docs/search-chrome-behaviour.md mandates, which was not added and is still required. OWNER DECISION PENDING on whether to do that work.
